thread:
Priya: Quick sync — we're drafting the dedicated capacity roadmap checkpoints for the next customer handshakes. Primary open decisions: 1) reserved-pool sizing calc (committed vs buffer), 2) burst admission policy (soft vs hard, carryover), 3) autoscale cooldown + prewarm behavior, 4) billing grace and downgrade windows. Who can own which?

Sam: I can take pool sizing. Need P95 latency target and session length distributions from CS.

Lina: From customers on pilot: median session ~45s, a long tail up to ~10min for heavy assistants. P95 token latency target for Dedicated is 200ms. A couple of mid-market customers explicitly asked for ~20% burst headroom.

Jordan: Ops note: prewarming GPUs is costly. Prefer a hybrid: scheduled prewarm windows for known peaks + predictive prewarm for gradual ramps. Also, autoscale cooldown shouldn't be <5m or we see thrash.

Alex: Sketching an autoscale policy we can try in staging:
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_nodes: 2
  max_nodes: 50
  scale_up:
    policy: add-on-threshold
    cpu_threshold: 70%
    queue_len_threshold: 10
  scale_down:
    policy: gradual-remove
    cpu_below: 40%
    sustained_for: 10m
  prewarm_window: 10m
```
This keeps cost bounded while giving short prewarm buffer.

Priya: Tradeoffs: longer scale_down reduces oscillation but delays reclaiming capacity (affects cost). If we add burst carryover semantics, billing/credits get more complex. We need a customer-facing guarantee for committed pools.

Sam: Proposal: split pool model — committed (SLA-backed) + opportunistic. Opportunistic gives soft-burst capacity; it can be preempted. Admission: soft admission for burst with a token-bucket over 5 minutes; if exceeded, spill traffic to opportunistic with a small latency penalty (~2s) or route to fallback model.

Lina: Important: customers want predictable billing language. Suggested launch criteria for the feature: (a) per-route SLOs met in staging for 2 weeks under synthetic mixed workloads, (b) billing telemetry consistent and <10% variance vs forecast during those runs, (c) CS playbook + docs published, (d) canary rollouts and rollback triggers defined.

Jordan: Add runbook items: graceful degradation path, automated fallback to smaller quantized model, and a quick region failover plan. Also include an emergency drain + eviction script for opportunistic workloads.

Priya: Agree. Action owners: @Sam own sizing + committed vs opportunistic split, @Alex own autoscale config + prewarm tuning, @Jordan runbook + region failover, @Lina finalize billing language and launch checklist. Can we target a draft decision matrix by EOD Friday?

Sam: Ack — I'll post a sizing spreadsheet and assumptions by Thursday.

Alex: Will prototype the autoscale policy in staging tomorrow and share CPU/latency traces.

Jordan: I'll draft the runbook, incl. a simple k8s drain command and rollback steps.

Lina: I'll draft the customer-facing billing FAQ and add examples of burst scenarios (how credits/overflow are charged).

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: dedicated-capacity-autoscale-proto -> staging at 2024-04-18 03:00 UTC :rocket:

Priya: Nice. One more decision: do we allow burst carryover across billing cycles (partial carryover) or force a per-window reset? My lean: allow small carryover (up to 10%) to reduce customer surprises, but require clear cap and expiry. Thoughts?

Sam: Small carryover with expiry sounds fair. We'll model worst-case cost impact in the spreadsheet.

Jordan: Carryover increases complexity for eviction logic. If we allow it, make it time-limited and non-transferrable across customer orgs.

Lina: Customers will like a buffer. We'll test messaging: "10% carryover for 48 hours" as an option in the contract.

Priya: Great. I'll collate decisions and put a lightweight decision matrix into the roadmap doc (committed sizing, opportunistic policy, autoscale config, carryover terms, launch criteria). We'll sync Friday for final sign-off. :thumbsup:
